issues: whether a business owner owes a duty of care to third parties injured as a result of a thief's negligent driving of a stolen vehicle
whether leaving a vehicle unlocked with keys inside on commercial premises breaches the standard of care owed to third parties
whether the intervening criminal act of theft breaks the chain of causation between the business's conduct and the passenger's injuries
whether theft of the vehicle and subsequent negligent driving causing injury was a reasonably foreseeable consequence of leaving keys in an unlocked car
whether the thief's status as a minor affects the foreseeability or novus actus interveniens analysis
what standard of care applies to a commercial garage or parking lot operator regarding security of vehicles on its premises
key_facts: a teenager stole an unlocked car with the keys left inside from a commercial garage lot
the thief crashed the stolen car
a passenger in the stolen car was seriously injured
the vehicle was located on the premises of a commercial garage business at the time of the theft
causes_of_action: occupiers' liability (if a premises-based duty applies)
search_terms: duty of care third party criminal acts
stolen vehicle negligence third party injury
intervening criminal act chain of causation
reasonable foreseeability of theft leading to accident
needs_clarification: In which province or jurisdiction did the theft, crash, and injury occur, since this is a provincial tort/negligence matter?
